title: Time Jump to 15:05: Third Truck Colour, SAR Wants Escorts

fields.scenarioTitle: North Gate — Fairgrounds Abduction, AMBER Decision & Unified Command
fields.narration: The clock moves forward to 15:05. It is now an hour since the first 911 call, and Lily Ashby is still missing. The AMBER worksheet is due for its 30-minute review. Deputy Wren 16 has just finished interviewing a third witness, a worker at a ride-ticket booth near the north gate. She says the pickup that went out the north gate was "gray, kind of a primer gray, not shiny." So far the truck has been described as dark, then dark blue, then gray. Nobody has reached the second caller from 14:16, who reported a girl in a purple coat at the food booths. That lead is still open. Festival visitors are starting to leave through the main gate and the north gate. At the Fire District 1 check-in point, the Wren County Search and Rescue coordinator walks up to Battalion Chief Rae Olson and says: "I've got 22 volunteers signed in. I need four deputies to escort teams through the barns and the RV area, and I need them now, before it gets dark." Patrol is fully committed. Two deputies are on the north gate road and the Highway 26 approach. The rest are posted at the gates and at Exhibit Hall B.
worldState: Time is 15:05. It has been 65 minutes since the 14:00 call on CAD 26-081377 and 85 minutes since Lily was last seen at 13:40 near the Exhibit Hall B petting area.
The AMBER worksheet's 30-minute review is due now.

The vehicle has now been described three ways: "dark pickup" from volunteer Marcy Delgado, then "dark blue, older, maybe a Ford" from the same volunteer, then "primer gray, not shiny" from a ride-ticket booth worker interviewed by Wren 16. The grandparent's public post says "silver-gray Chevy." No witness has a plate.
The departure time is still estimated at 13:45 to 13:55.
The 14:16 food-booth sighting (girl in a purple coat near the kettle corn stand at about 14:05, alone) has not been called back at 541-555-0117 and is still open.
Visitors are leaving through the main gate and the north gate. About 3,000 people were on the grounds at 14:05.

Wren County Search and Rescue has 22 volunteers signed in at the Fire District 1 check-in point. The coordinator is asking for four deputy escorts for the barns and the RV area. Sunset is at about 18:20.
On patrol there are 5 deputies and 1 sergeant. Two deputies are on the north gate road and the Highway 26 approach, and the rest are at the gates and Exhibit Hall B. No deputy is free.
APD, Fire District 1 and OSP commanders are at the Exhibit Hall B command post. KWRN-TV's live broadcast at 15:00 has already gone out.
fields.facilitatorNote: Watch whether the IC runs the worksheet review inside unified command and marks each of the five criteria yes or no with a reason, as WCSO-SOP-12 section 4 requires. The IC should also name who chases each gap: INV on the vehicle description and COMMS on the food-booth call-back. The SAR escort request should be met through Fire District 1 staging and APD or mutual aid officers, without pulling deputies off the vehicle search. Prompt the Undersheriff on an off-duty callout, or on a Deschutes/Jefferson request made in the order WCICMA section 5 sets.

instructorNote: This card moves the clock 15 minutes, from 14:50 to 15:05, and adds pressure to the AMBER review with a third truck colour and an open sighting while SAR competes for scarce deputies. Look for a criterion-by-criterion review with named owners for each gap, SAR escorts drawn from APD or mutual aid rather than the vehicle search, and an Undersheriff decision on a callout or a neighbor-county request.
